(1) It enforces a domain rule: the 1–300 capacity check in create() is a Course rule and belongs in the domain layer. (2) It changes state directly on the persistence record: publish() sets entity.published = true on the TypeORM CourseEntity instead of asking the domain Course to change its own state. (3) It does persistence work itself. It builds TypeORM queries (findOne/find with where clauses, create/save) and exports the toCourse mapper, which converts the ORM entity into the domain object. That mapping and query code belongs in an infrastructure repository or adapter. Calling a repository is normal for an application service. Building ORM queries and mapping entities, alongside domain rules, is not. I did not judge import direction, which is out of scope.
